title: flake_fix@1: a build spec that fixes a flaky test and is verified by repeated reruns

story.i_want_to: a test-flakiness issue that chg's master verifier files to be fixed by a spec agent and verified by rerunning the test under load on another runner
story.so_that: the 45 HCB flaky-test issues a month stop costing sessions and CI re-runs

rationale: US-48.15 ranked this second. chg already files each flake with its record and a KB finding; the verifier criterion is mechanical. It is also the second :build spec, the PRD's test that a new agent needs no new loopctl modules.

acceptance_criteria.description: Registry entry flake_fix@1 with archetype :build, candidates admitted by the test-flakiness label (US-49.1's admit_labels), and its own runner template {id, version}; adding it creates no new loopctl module outside lib/loopctl/agents/specs/.

The spec's merge-gate screen refuses a diff that touches files outside test/** and test/support/**, adds @tag :skip or @moduletag :skip, deletes a test, or raises a timeout without a code change beside it; a refused diff escalates over merge_gate.

The verify dispatch for a flake_fix story carries the test id and a rerun count (default 30, a per-tenant knob that cannot move authority); the verifier passes only when every rerun is green at the recorded head.

The outcome row records merged, reverted, verify verdict, and recurred: true when a new test-flakiness issue names the same test file and test name within 14 days of the merge, from the intake event, never from session text.
Eval cases (US-48.10) for flake_fix@1 are synthetic: a time-of-day test, a shared-state test, a load timeout.

test_cases.name: recurrence is recorded from intake
steps: deliver a new test-flakiness issue naming the same test 3 days later
expected_results: recurred true on the original row

test_cases.name: registry test holds the kind lists equal
expected_results: flake_fix appears in RunnerContract.Kinds and the ledger kind CHECK

technical_notes: A flake whose cause is in lib/ (a real race) is out of scope by design: the screen escalates it, and a human routes it as a deferred-finding.
The rerun belongs to the verifier, so the implementer's own green reruns count for nothing (no self-certification).
